scope: Repair unsafe standalone normal termination found by unchanged broad Node tests. Linux x64; full-suite and cross-platform completion are not claimed.
findings: The previous direct host libc exit call bypassed engine shutdown. A fresh immutable Node campaign passed 59 tests and failed three (445, 452, 4534) before a checkpointed pause.

GDB traced 452 to SIGABRT in uv_mutex_destroy called by libc exit handlers while Node worker threads were still live. This is a Lasm shutdown bug, not an OOM, and the debugger run itself is diagnostic evidence, not a test pass.

Ordinary standalone exit now awaits fflush(NULL) from the same CRT as the Lean FILE streams and then calls the engine process.exit. Forced exit still calls native _Exit without flushing. Embedded guests keep their existing exception contract.
Only two private host modules changed in the derived snapshots; all Wasm, Lean, SDK, and dispatcher inputs are unchanged.
All three original failing tests pass under Node, Deno, and Bun. Native and all three full runtimes also match exact return/exit/force status, stdout, stderr, and open-file bytes.
A small independent background-compilation probe passed both before and after the fix. It did not reproduce the defect and is not counted as regression evidence.
All original-source checks passed and all OOM, cap-hit, throttling, and swap counters were zero. Memory budgets were not raised.
